entities.name: PMID:25450181
observations: 2015 study, “Metabolic control analysis of the Trypanosoma cruzi peroxide detoxification pathway identifies tryparedoxin as a suitable drug target.” Reconstituted the pathway in vitro and quantified flux control.

entities.name: Tryparedoxin (TXN)
observations: The study proposed TXN as a drug target based on high control of peroxide-detoxification flux, low catalytic efficiency, and its role in supplying reducing equivalents to TXNPx and GPxA.

entities.name: T. cruzi peroxide detoxification
observations: In vitro reconstituted pathway examined in the MCA includes TryR, TXN, and the TXNPx and GPxA redox pairs.

entities.name: TXN redox-pair control
observations: In the reconstituted in-vitro pathway, TXN–TXNPx and TXN–GPxA redox pairs together exerted 90–100% control of peroxide-detoxification flux; TryR exerted about 10%. The abstract does not report separate individual enzyme coefficients.
This is mechanistic target rationale, not proof that inhibiting TXN is effective or selective in infected cells or animals.
